title: The Warrior Not Yet Chosen
summary: A Valkyrie stops beside a fallen warrior. Her answer is not the one he expects.
author: T.R. Pomeroy
source_title: Ep. Beta 002 - Valkyries and Viking Visions of the Afterlife
paragraphs: A warrior stumbles, sword slipping from blood-slick fingers. The battle rages, but his world is fading—cold creeping through his limbs, the sky turning to shadow. Then, a gust of wind. Wings. Figures descend from the storm, their armor glinting like ice, eyes burning with something not of this world. The Valkyries. Their voices weave through the chaos, naming the fallen, deciding who will rise again in Odin’s hall—and who will be forgotten.

The warrior’s breath falters. Will they choose him? Will he feast in Valhalla, or be cast into the depths of Hel? One Valkyrie turns, locking eyes with him. She speaks. But her words are not what he expected. "You are not ready." The words strike harder than any blade. Not ready? The warrior’s mouth fills with blood and disbelief. Not ready? After all he’s done? After every wound, every scream, every friend buried in the mud?

His chest heaves, not with breath—but rage. He tries to rise, but his limbs betray him. The ground beneath is cold. Wet. Final. The Valkyrie’s gaze doesn’t waver. She is not cruel. She is not kind. She simply is—a force older than stone. The chooser of the slain. "You sought glory," she says, her voice a wind through winter trees, "but you feared pain. You struck true—but not first. You waited. You doubted."

She kneels beside him, close enough now that the light in her eyes blinds him. "There are worse things than death. Worse even than Hel’s gates. The forgotten… they become shadows. They wander, hungry. They rot, but do not rest. That is not your fate—yet." He tries to speak. His throat works, but no words come. Only a rasp. A plea. She touches two fingers to his chest. His heart stirs. Not strongly. But it stirs.

"Rise again," she whispers. "Earn the song. Fight until the gods cannot ignore your name." She stands. The wind lifts her cloak. The storm swells. All around them, warriors are being lifted from death— eyes blazing, wounds forgotten. But not him. Not yet. The Valkyrie disappears into the sky. And the lone warrior lies breathing. Bleeding. Burning. Still alive. He stares up at the empty sky where the Valkyrie vanished, her words echoing louder than the war drums ever did.

"Rise again." "Earn the song." His body screams with pain. Every rib feels cracked, his leg twisted beneath him, his sword a shattered memory beside his fingers. And yet… he is still here. Still breathing. Around him, the battlefield exhales its final breath. A shield lies splintered over a fallen friend’s face. A spear still quivers in the throat of a war horse. The wind moves through the dead like a priest through a chapel— quiet, reverent, cruel.

He turns his head with effort, his cheek grinding against the mud. There—just yards away—another warrior, eyes wide open but unseeing, mouth still caught in a scream that would never end. A boy. Barely grown. His axe too large for his hands. No Valkyrie came for him. And yet, the wind had whispered other names. Men he knew. Men no braver than he. But they had been chosen.

Not him. A great silence presses on his chest, heavier than the dying sun above. The silence of not being enough. But somewhere beneath that weight, something stirs. Not pride. Not anger. Resolve. If he was not enough— he would become enough. If the sagas did not yet sing his name— he would give them reason to. He clenches his fist. Pain floods him, but he welcomes it. Pain means life. Life means another chance.

The sun breaks through the clouds, just a sliver, catching on the hilt of a forgotten sword in the dirt. Not his own. Better. He crawls. Every inch of movement feels like fire through bone. But he moves. Because he has not been claimed. And that means—he still has a say. He drags the sword to his chest and lies still, breath rattling. The wind quiets. The ravens return.

One lands near him, tilting its head. Watching. Waiting. In the distance, the last of the living gather. A few rise, bruised and bloodied, looking around as if waking from a dream. The warrior watches them. He wonders if they saw the Valkyries too. He wonders if they felt that same icy judgment pierce their soul. "You are not ready." The words burn again—but now, they burn as fuel.
Because one day, when the sky darkens and the wind howls, when wings thunder once more over a blood-soaked field, he will do his best to be ready. But he still wonders if she will call his name.
context: An imagined encounter on a battlefield, inspired by the valkyries of Norse myth. The warrior’s second chance and the Valkyrie’s judgment are elements of this original story, not a recorded Norse rule about who reaches Valhalla.
editorial_note: Selected from the author’s manuscript. Broadcast transitions and pronunciation cues have been removed; paragraph breaks and obvious transcription slips have been adjusted for reading.
